headline: Excitebike hands you the exit
lede: Your own designs now walk you home: a saved custom track chosen at the splash grows an on-screen EXIT button, and Esc or the tap drops you back into the design bay with the course loaded byte-for-byte — while the league's six tracks keep their full-race promise, and test rides keep the ABANDON badge the QA lane shipped this afternoon.

notes.text: ONE LAW, THREE DOORS — ownTerrain(i): the bay's TEST draft and every registered custom are YOURS, so riding one grows the pad's third button (ABANDON on test rides, EXIT on your saved designs); Esc rides the same law from the keyboard. Tracks 1-6 stay a real race: no button, no escape.

What you edit is what you rode: abandoning mid-custom reads the seated entry's own stamps, so the bay reopens with terrain byte-identical to the lap you just left — and walking out submits nothing, the leaderboard stays the league's (pinned structural: the pure sim cannot even touch storage).

excitecheck 363/363 with a new OWN EXIT block (law x13, reload byte-identity x2 customs, submit-nothing), 427/427 mutants dead plus two by-hand structural mutants killed by name; exciteplay 103/103 driving the QA lane's six ABANDON gates and thirteen new own-exit legs side by side in one browser session, zero page errors.

Two lanes shipped the same corner of the shelf today and the merge shows it: QA's #2606 (candidate 7) landed minutes before our #2605 (candidates 7+8) — theirs kept verbatim, this PR generalizes the law and records the supersession in the README. A collision handled as a delta, not a revert.
